subject: Question re regression with noisy observation

messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: Question re regression with noisy observation
parts:
Dear all,

In the doc, it was shown how to do regression with y ~ normal (beta * x, sigma) where x ~ some kind of distribution.

In a slight variation, I have the following data:

noise free: y noisy: x ~ normal (x_mu, x_sigma)

model:
delta(y) ~ normal (beta * delta(x), sigma)

If i just code it up naively:

int N_1;
vector[N] delta_y;
vector[N] delta_x;

N_1 = N+1;
delta_y = y[2:N_1] - y[1:N];
delta_x = x[2:N_1] - x[1:N];

delta_y ~ normal (beta * delta_x, sigma);
x ~ normal (x_mu, x_sigma);
beta ~ normal (0, 1);

I would observe quite a lot of divergent transition. I think the underlying issue is the choice of Xs are not independent of each other.

My question is: What would be a good re-parametrization approach that could work?

many thanks!

Andy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question re regression with noisy observation
parts:
You want to turn this around and ask yourself how the data
comes about. I think what you're saying is that you
have an independent model for some underlying x, and
then instead of modeling y based on x, you model change in
y based on change in x.

There's nothing wrong with that model per se, but it's unusual.
And it doesn't give you a model of the first y. A more
common approach to doing this is to take a moving average type
time series model, where

x[n + 1] ~ normal(x[n] | mu, sigma);

y[n + 1] ~ normal(y[n + 1] | phi, tau);

To answer your direct question, what you want to do is non-center
this bit:

x ~ normal (x_mu, x_sigma);

replacing it with

x_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

x = x_mu + x_raw * x_sigma;

- Bob
